title: Interpreting the Meaning of the Derivative in Context
core_idea: A derivative in context is a rate of change with units and a specific meaning tied to the quantities in the problem.
what_students_need_to_understand: FRQs frequently award points for interpretation, not only computation, and the wording must match the scenario.
how_this_becomes_points: You earn points by stating what is changing, with respect to what, at what input, and in what units.

title: Approximating Values of a Function Using Local Linearity and Linearization
core_idea: Linearization uses the tangent line near a point to approximate nearby function values.
what_students_need_to_understand: AP questions use this to connect derivatives to approximation, error reasoning, and readable tangent-line equations.
how_this_becomes_points: You earn points by building L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x-a), substituting the nearby input, and stating that it is an approximation.
answer_move: Find f(a) and f'(a), write the tangent-line model, then evaluate the nearby x-value.
